# `scope_send_cmd`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Guider: forward a raw command to the mount controller (generic passthrough).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider dispatcher table, handler @0x80160 (64-bit guider build; driver SendCmd @0xf1030, MethodRetSwitch<string>), @0x78438 (32-bit build); static analysis of app 3.3.2, BaseDeviceViewModel.getBacklashDeg and setBacklashDeg, SetBacklashDegParams |

Guider generic command passthrough. Registered in the guider dispatcher table; on 4700 it is reached through the imager method-not-found relay (mount-and-motion R1, R2). READ: params are positional [cmd, resp] or keyed {cmd, resp}. cmd (string, required; missing or non-string gives 105) is written raw to the mount controller, which needs a connected mount (315; a disconnected driver gives 318). resp selects how the reply is read: a string reads up to the terminator given by its first character (32-byte buffer); a positive integer n reads n bytes (fewer is a failure); an integer of 0 or less reads one byte and, if it is 'e', reads on to '#' and returns that text, else returns "0"; absent or another type reads nothing and returns "". The result is the reply text as a string, or {"value": text} with ret_obj true. Write or read failures reply with the thread error code (no specific code). The app uses it to read and set backlash, so it can change mount configuration or move the mount; graded MUTATOR / tier C. A client SHOULD NOT send controller strings it does not understand.

Side effects: Writes cmd raw to the mount controller and reads its reply; depending on the command this can change mount configuration or move the mount. READ the write; INFERRED the possible effects.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_send_cmd"`. [READ] |
| `params` | array\|object | no | - | Positional [cmd, resp] or keyed {cmd, resp, ret_obj}. cmd: string written raw to the controller (required, 105 if missing or not a string). resp: optional; a string gives the reply terminator (its first character), a positive integer a byte count, an integer of 0 or less a one-byte 'e'-test read; absent or another type means no read. ret_obj true wraps the result as {"value": text}. The app sends [command, "#"] for a read and {cmd, resp: 1, ret_obj: 1} for a write. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | cmd missing or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 315 | No mount is connected | `mount is not connected` |
| 318 | The mount driver is not connected | `device not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

Write or read failures (including a short fixed-length read) reply with the thread error code, which the driver does not set to a specific value; those codes are not exhausted by this table.

## Example

Request, list-form - List form as the app builds it for a read (command text invented):

```json
{"id":121,"method":"scope_send_cmd","params":[":XX#","#"]}
```

Request, object-form - Object form as the app builds it for a write (command text invented):

```json
{"id":122,"method":"scope_send_cmd","params":{"cmd":":XX5#","resp":1,"ret_obj":1}}
```

Reply, ok-string - Reply to the list form (reply text invented):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_send_cmd","result":"12","code":0,"id":121}
```
